issues.description: Race condition on is_registered flag allows missing LoRA weights on concurrent first-use requests
issues.detail: In _create_trtllm_generate_request, the code checks lora_config.is_registered, loads weights, then sets the flag. With async/concurrent requests, two simultaneous first requests may both see is_registered=False and proceed, but worse: there is no lock, so one request can set is_registered=True before the other sends weights to the backend, causing the backend to receive only task_id with no cached registration yet.

issues.description: Shared mutable TritonLoraConfig.is_registered state is unsafe across model reloads and process restarts
issues.detail: lora_config.is_registered is set on the metadata object cached in self.model_metadata. If the Triton model is reloaded or the LoRA cache is evicted on the backend side, the frontend still believes it's registered and will only send task_id, causing backend errors. There is no invalidation path.

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path reassigned inside loop overwrites the multi_lora.json path
issues.detail: At line ~659, lora_config_path is set to version_path/multi_lora.json. Then inside the loop over lora_config.items(), lora_config_path is reassigned to lora_path/model.lora_config.npy. On subsequent iterations of the outer repo_paths loop this shadowed value would be used incorrectly. Rename one of them.

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production code paths
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside _parse_lora_configs loop and print(traceback.format_exc()) in the exception handler and in all three FastAPI routers (chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py) will spam stdout in production. Use proper logging at appropriate levels instead of print.

issues.description: _get_lora_config can crash with AttributeError when model_name is unknown
issues.detail: self.model_metadata.get(model_name) returns None if model_name is missing, then model_metadata.lora_configs raises AttributeError instead of a clean ClientError. Should validate model_metadata is not None before accessing attributes.

issues.description: Return type annotation of _parse_lora_configs is incorrect
issues.detail: The signature declares return type `None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but the function actually returns `List[TritonLoraConfig]` or None. Update the annotation to match the actual return type to avoid misleading future maintainers and static analysis.

review.summary: The PR adds multi-LoRA support to the TensorRT-LLM backend in the OpenAI-compatible frontend. The main concerns are a race condition around the is_registered flag during concurrent first-use requests, brittle shared mutable state with no invalidation when the backend cache evicts, a variable shadowing bug for lora_config_path, debug prints left in production paths, and a minor null-safety gap in _get_lora_config. Type annotations also drift from actual return types. Tests were broadened but rely on environmental detection of the backend, which may reduce coverage where both backends are present.
